title: Midnight Mass (Luke 2:1–14)

lines: A CHURCH AT AN ODD HOUR.
cards: It's late on Christmas Eve. The presents are wrapped, or they aren't. The kids are asleep, or coming along in pajamas under their coats.
And people walk into a church at an hour when nothing else is open, to hear a story that also happens at night. The church is dim, then lit.
The Gloria, left out on the Sundays of Advent, comes back, and in some parishes bells ring with it. At church, Christmas begins in the dark.

teach.b: The Roman Missal gives Christmas four Masses: the vigil in the evening, the Mass during the night, the Mass at dawn and the Mass during the day. The night one is what people call Midnight Mass, and its gospel is Luke 2.
Luke starts with an emperor. Caesar Augustus orders the whole world enrolled, and Joseph and Mary, who is with child, travel to Bethlehem because of a decree from Rome.
Power at the top of the world, two people at the bottom. The birth takes one sentence.

In the Douay-Rheims: "And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him up in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn." A manger is a feeding trough.

Then Luke turns to the night shift: shepherds in the fields, keeping the night watches over their flock. An angel appears, the glory of the Lord shines round about them, and they're terrified. Fear not, the angel says.
Then a multitude of angels praises God with the line the Gloria at Mass begins with: "Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will."
An honest note: Luke never gives the hour of the birth.

teach.h: GLORY TO GOD IN THE HIGHEST.
teach.b: Tradition ties this Mass to the night because Luke sets the shepherds there, and because an old Christmas-season chant borrows a line from the book of Wisdom: God's word leaping down from heaven while all things were in quiet silence and the night was half gone.
The darkness is the point. The light shows up where people are working the night shift.

how: Catholic parishes celebrate the Mass during the Night on Christmas Eve, sometimes at midnight and often earlier, with Luke 2:1–14 as the gospel and the Gloria sung again after Advent.

games.q: you're a shepherd. the angels have sung and gone, and the sky is dark again. what do you do?
o: go back to sleep; it was a dream.
say, let us go to Bethlehem and see.

games.why: they go to Bethlehem in haste and find Mary, Joseph and the infant lying in the manger (Luke 2:15–16).

practice: Turn off what you can, and if it's dark where you are, leave it dark a moment, then light one small light.

Picture the field outside Bethlehem: cold, sheep shifting, a few tired workers awake while everyone else sleeps, and then the light. If you pray, say the angels' line, glory to God in the highest; if not, let the quiet be full.

wordCard.voice: Midnight Mass. The Christmas Mass during the night, where Luke's story of the birth and the shepherds is read in the dark. Today's word.
